metaDescription: Six countertop ice makers listed at or below $300, mostly nugget models plus a crescent maker, compared on output, first batch time and cleaning.
expertTake: The EUHOMY 44 lb nugget maker is the top pick for the highest output and a 7 to 10 minute first batch. The Frigidaire V2 is the value pick for a plain nugget maker from a known brand. Skip nugget if you want hard, slow melting cubes, since the crescent maker suits that better.
introParagraphs: At this cap the market is dominated by countertop nugget makers, the soft chewable ice that many people want at home. The choice is mostly between output, first batch time and extras such as a touchscreen or a dispenser.

This guide compares those machines and one crescent maker for people who prefer hard cubes. Rated output is a best case, so we look at basket size, cycle time and how easy each unit is to clean. Prices move, so the $300 cap reflects listing prices when this guide was updated.

products.name: EUHOMY nugget ice maker, 44 lb per day, ready in 7 to 10 min
products.description:
The EUHOMY 44 lb is a countertop nugget maker with first ice in 7 to 10 minutes and a rating of 44 pounds a day. It includes a scoop and a self cleaning cycle. It is rated higher than most countertop nugget units.

The extra output over the 33 lb Frigidaire units is a real step for a busy household. It is a compact all rounder. Its 44 lb rating tops the Frigidaire V2's 33 lb, with a faster first batch.

Descale it on schedule and empty the water before storage. Leave clearance around it. Before relying on the EUHOMY 44 lb nugget for a party, run it for an hour and note how much ice it really makes in your room, since rated output assumes cool air and cold water.
products.bestFor: Households that want the highest nugget output here

products.name: Frigidaire EFIC239 countertop nugget ice maker V2, 33 lb
products.description:
The Frigidaire V2 is a countertop nugget maker rated at 33 pounds a day, with first ice in about 15 minutes. It makes soft, crunchy, chewable ice of the kind sold at drive throughs. It plugs in and needs no plumbing.

The 15 minute first batch is slower than the 6 or 7 minutes of some rivals. It is a straightforward, well known brand in a plain package. Its 33 lb rating and 15 minute first batch are plainer than the EUHOMY's.

Descale it every month or two and empty the reservoir before storage. Leave clearance around it. Plan where the Frigidaire nugget V2 will sit, with clear space around it and a flat, level surface, because blocked vents are the usual cause of weak output.
products.bestFor: Households that want brand name nugget ice
cons: Slower first batch than some rivals
Nugget machines are louder than bullet makers

products.name: Frigidaire touchscreen nugget ice maker, 33 lb capacity
products.description:
The Frigidaire touchscreen nugget maker is rated at 33 pounds and adds an intelligent touchscreen control panel and automatic cleaning. It makes light, crunchy nugget ice. The touchscreen is the difference from the plain V2.

It gives you the same output with a nicer panel. The panel is the extra that you pay for. It matches the V2's 33 lb and adds a touchscreen and automatic cleaning.

Descale it on schedule and wipe the screen with a soft cloth. Leave clearance around it. Use filtered or distilled water in the Frigidaire touchscreen nugget if your tap water is hard, as scale on the evaporator cuts output and makes ice taste flat.
products.bestFor: Households that want a touchscreen and nugget ice
cons: Panel adds cost over the V2

products.name: EUHOMY nugget ice maker countertop, 40 lb per 24 hours, sonic ice
products.description:
The EUHOMY 40 lb is a countertop nugget maker with a 7 minute first batch and a rating of 40 pounds a day. It offers one touch controls and a self cleaning cycle. It makes crunchy pellet ice.

It sits between the 33 lb and 44 lb units. The fast first batch is its selling point. Its 7 minute first batch beats the Frigidaire units' 15 minutes.

Descale it on schedule and empty the water before storage. Keep the manual for the EUHOMY 40 lb nugget nearby, since the descaling method and the standing time after a move are the two details owners most often miss.
products.bestFor: Households that want fast nugget ice at mid output

products.name: ecozy nugget ice maker countertop dispenser, 40 lb per day
products.description:
The ecozy is a slim countertop nugget maker with touch free dispensing and a 40 pound rating. You place a cup under the chute and press a button. It targets kitchens, dorms and RVs.

The dispenser means you never open a lid, which keeps the ice cleaner. It costs more than a plain basket unit. It adds touch free dispensing to a 40 lb nugget maker.

Descale it on schedule and wipe the chute. Leave clearance around it. Empty and dry the ecozy nugget dispenser before storage or a long trip, because standing water grows slime in the reservoir within days.
cons: Dispenser adds a part to clean

products.name: EUHOMY countertop crescent ice maker, 35 lb, 16 cubes in 12 min
products.description:
The EUHOMY crescent maker produces 16 slow melting crescent cubes in 12 minutes, at 35 pounds a day. It offers a timer, adjustable ice thickness and automatic deep cleaning. Crescent cubes melt slower than bullets.

The 12 minute cycle is slower than a bullet maker, and the output is a little higher. It suits people who want a cube that holds up in a glass. It makes slow melting crescent cubes, unlike the nugget picks.

Descale on schedule and empty the water before storage. Leave clearance around it. Write down how often you refill the EUHOMY crescent maker during a typical week, as that number tells you quickly whether its tank size suits your habits.
products.bestFor: Drinkers who want slow melting crescent cubes
cons: 12 minute cycle is slower than bullets

buyingCriteria.explanation: Countertop units refill by hand from a 1.1 to 1.8 L reservoir and need no plumbing, which suits renters and RVs. Undercounter commercial style units store a lot more ice and make far more, but need a drain, a water supply and clearance. Frigidaire nugget V2 and EUHOMY 40 lb nugget show the difference in this lineup. Plumbing is the real cost of the larger category.

buyingCriteria.criterion: First batch time and cycle length
buyingCriteria.explanation: The first batch usually takes 6 to 15 minutes, and later cycles repeat every 6 to 8 minutes, filling a basket in under an hour. A listing that quotes 6 or 7 minutes is describing the first cycle. EUHOMY 44 lb nugget and Frigidaire touchscreen nugget quote different times in this lineup. Time to first ice matters for parties, while daily output matters for steady use.

Compressor units need breathing room, often 6 inches or more on all sides, and a blocked unit makes less ice and wears faster. Noise is compressor hum plus cubes dropping, roughly like a mini fridge for bullet makers and louder for nugget makers with an auger. Frigidaire nugget V2 and EUHOMY 40 lb nugget are the picks to place with care. Do not put one in a cabinet with no airflow.

Hard water leaves scale on the evaporator, which cuts output and flavour. Filtered or distilled water slows the build up, and descaling with citric acid or a manufacturer approved cleaner every month or two removes what a self clean cycle does not. EUHOMY 44 lb nugget (44 lb nugget) and Frigidaire touchscreen nugget (33 lb nugget, touchscreen) both need this routine. Skipping it is the most common reason output falls over time.

Portable ice makers do not keep ice frozen: melt water drains back to the reservoir and is recycled, so the ice is for immediate use. Insulated bins slow melting but do not stop it. Frigidaire nugget V2 (33 lb nugget, 15 min) and EUHOMY 40 lb nugget (40 lb nugget) handle storage differently. If you want ice ready all day, look at bin size and insulation.

Touchscreens, timers and app control are conveniences, while a self cleaning cycle flushes the reservoir but does not remove scale. Some nugget units add a dispenser so you can fill a cup without opening the lid. EUHOMY 44 lb nugget and EUHOMY 40 lb nugget differ on controls. Choose the features you will use daily, not a long list.

specDecoder.meaning: The amount of ice the basket or bin holds. Countertop baskets hold about 1 to 2 pounds, and commercial bins hold much more.
specDecoder.watchFor: Check the stated bin size for EUHOMY 40 lb nugget.

specDecoder.meaning: The water tank of a countertop unit, often 1.1 to 1.8 L. A small tank means more refills during a party.
specDecoder.watchFor: See whether EUHOMY 44 lb nugget states its tank size.

specDecoder.meaning: Nugget is soft and chewable, bullet is hard and slow melting, and crescent is clear and curved. The shape affects taste and melt rate.
specDecoder.watchFor: Note which shape Frigidaire nugget V2 makes before buying.

specDecoder.meaning: A safety mark shows the unit was assessed to a recognised standard. It matters most for undercounter units installed in a home.
specDecoder.watchFor: Look for it on EUHOMY 40 lb nugget.

specDecoder.meaning: The time for the first cycle, usually 6 to 15 minutes. Later cycles are similar but a full basket stops production.
specDecoder.watchFor: Read how Frigidaire touchscreen nugget quotes its first batch.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ice type and use
howWeEvaluated.description: We matched nugget, bullet, crescent and cube styles to how people drink. We avoided ranking different ice types on output alone. Frigidaire touchscreen nugget and EUHOMY 40 lb nugget represent different types in this lineup.

howWeEvaluated.title: Installation and clearance
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at drain needs, water supply and the clearance each unit demands. A unit that fits your space gets used. Frigidaire nugget V2 was the reference for a different installation style.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cleaning and descaling
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked for self cleaning cycles and notes on descaling. We favoured designs with accessible reservoirs and trays. EUHOMY 44 lb nugget was set against the others on this point.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at what owners repeatedly report, not at any one summary figure. Repeated complaints about noise, leaks or output lowered a pick. This guide quotes no star figures or review totals, and no such number fed the ranking.

howWeEvaluated.title: Output and basket realism
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated daily output with basket size and cycle time, and treated output as a best case. EUHOMY 44 lb nugget at 44 lb nugget and Frigidaire nugget V2 at 33 lb nugget, 15 min were compared this way.

howToChoose.intro: Decide first whether ice is a daily habit or an occasional need, and whether you have a drain nearby. Countertop units refill by hand and need no plumbing, while commercial style units need water and drainage. The rows below map common situations to the picks in this lineup, including Frigidaire nugget V2.

rows: You want nugget ice from a known brand
You want to dispense into a cup

howToChoose.note: Whichever you choose, leave clearance around the unit, since the compressor needs air and a crowded cabinet cuts both output and lifespan.

howToChoose.intro: Every pick here is listed at or below the $300 cap, so the tiers below are relative to each other, not to the cap.

rows: Spending the least this lineup allows
EUHOMY crescent maker (35 lb crescent) costs the least in this lineup, so it suits a buyer who wants working ice and little else.
Frigidaire touchscreen nugget (33 lb nugget, touchscreen) sits mid lineup on cost, balancing output, storage and ice type.
EUHOMY 40 lb nugget (40 lb nugget) costs the most in this lineup, so it needs to earn that premium on output, storage or build.

howToChoose.note: Treat the tiers as relative: a mid priced pick usually balances output and storage, while the cheapest suits light use and the dearest suits regular entertaining.

cards.label: Nugget ice
cards.text: The group of EUHOMY 44 lb nugget, Frigidaire nugget V2, Frigidaire touchscreen nugget, EUHOMY 40 lb nugget, and ecozy nugget dispenser makes nugget ice. It is soft and chewable and absorbs drink flavour, but the machines are heavier, louder and pricier. It suits people who chew ice.

cards.label: Cube, bullet or crescent ice
cards.text: The group of EUHOMY crescent maker makes harder, slower melting cubes. Hard cubes hold up in a drink and melt more slowly, and the machines are usually quieter. It suits people who want cold drinks that stay cold.

howToChoose.note: Pick nugget if you love chewing ice. Pick cubes if you want slower melting ice and a quieter, cheaper machine.

howToChoose.subheading: By Ice Type and Machine Style

rows: You want slow melting crescent cubes for drinks
A crescent maker produces clear, curved cubes that melt slowly, at a slightly lower output than a bullet maker of the same size.
You love soft, chewable pebble ice
EUHOMY 44 lb nugget, Frigidaire nugget V2, Frigidaire touchscreen nugget, EUHOMY 40 lb nugget, and ecozy nugget dispenser
A nugget maker scrapes ice from a cold cylinder and compresses it, which makes soft ice that absorbs drink flavour, in a heavier and louder machine.

howToChoose.subheading: For Parties and Summer Entertaining Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for a high rated output, a basket or bin that holds enough for a party, a fast first batch and a way to refill without waiting. Storage matters more than the daily total, since a party draws a lot of ice in an hour. A scoop and an easy basket also help.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: EUHOMY 44 lb nugget is the pick that best matches those points here, with 44 lb nugget. Frigidaire nugget V2 and Frigidaire touchscreen nugget are the nearest alternatives if you want a different ice type or a different mix of output and storage.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Spend more if you entertain often, want nugget ice, or need a bin that holds hours of ice. Stepping up to EUHOMY 40 lb nugget (40 lb nugget) buys the output or storage that cheaper units lack.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save if you want a few drinks a day or ice for an occasional trip. EUHOMY crescent maker (35 lb crescent) covers the basics, and a small difference in output rarely justifies a larger premium.

maintenance.task: Replace the water filter if fitted
maintenance.why: A saturated filter stops working and can leave off flavours. Follow the interval for your unit.
Dust blocks airflow to the compressor. A brush or a vacuum nozzle keeps the vents open.

maintenance.interval: After each use or before storage
maintenance.why: Standing water grows biofilm within days. Drain the tank and leave the lid open to dry.
Scale cuts output and flavour. Use citric acid or a manufacturer approved cleaner, then rinse well.
Residue and slime collect where ice sits. A mild soap solution keeps them clean.

faq.q: Is nugget ice worth the extra cost?
faq.a: If you love soft, chewable ice, yes, since nugget makers are the only way to get it at home. They are heavier, louder and pricier than bullet makers. A pick like Frigidaire nugget V2 shows how they differ.

faq.q: Why is my ice maker making less ice than rated?
faq.a: Warm rooms, warm water, blocked vents and scale all cut output. Check clearance and descale if the unit is a few months old. A cool room and filtered water help.

faq.q: Do I need a drain for an ice maker?
faq.a: Countertop units do not, but undercounter commercial style units usually do. Check the installation notes before buying one. EUHOMY 40 lb nugget is an example of a larger unit that needs planning.

faq.q: Can I move an ice maker after using it?
faq.a: Yes, but let it stand upright for a few hours before powering on so compressor oil settles. Empty the water first. This applies to every compressor based unit in this guide.

faq.q: Is a countertop ice maker loud?
faq.a: Bullet makers run roughly like a mini fridge, while nugget makers are louder because of the auger and compressor. Placement matters, and so does the surface under it. A unit like EUHOMY 44 lb nugget is worth reading about in owner notes.

faq.q: Why does this guide stop at $300?
faq.a: The $300 cap is the search keyword shoppers use, and every pick here was listed at or below it when this guide was updated. EUHOMY crescent maker is the cheapest option in this lineup and EUHOMY 40 lb nugget is the dearest, so the spread inside the cap is real. Prices move, so check the listing before you buy.
